title: How an X-Ray Machine Works in 60 Seconds ☢️🦴 #shorts
description:
An X-ray tube fires electrons from a hot filament into a spinning tungsten target at high voltage. Only about 1% of that energy becomes X-rays; the rest turns into heat. Bones absorb more X-rays than soft tissue, so they leave a bright shadow on the detector. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#xray #science #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: In an X-ray tube, about *99 percent* of the energy turns into *heat*.

steps.label: Filament
steps.text: A tiny *filament* glows white hot and boils off a cloud of *electrons*.

steps.label: Voltage
steps.text: Huge *voltage* slams those electrons across a vacuum toward a *tungsten* target.

steps.label: X-rays
steps.text: As they crash and brake, they throw off *X-rays*. The target *spins* so it won't melt.

steps.label: Body
steps.text: X-rays pass through *soft tissue*, but dense *bone* blocks far more of them.

steps.label: Detector
steps.text: A *detector* behind you catches what gets through, so bones show up *bright*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Electrons, target, *shadow*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
